characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. assamica (large-leaf Yunnan trees)

description.short: Yunnan white tea with two-toned leaves — dark on top and silvery underneath, fuller-bodied and more honeyed than Fujian white tea
description.overview: Crafted using white tea techniques but made from large-leaf Yunnan trees (Camellia sinensis var. assamica) rather than Fujian cultivars, resulting in a denser body and greater richness compared to traditional Fujian white tea.
description.leaf: Leaves with striking two-toned coloration: dark upper surface and silvery-white downy underside (hence 'Moonlight')
description.liquor: Golden-yellow liquor, deeper and richer than Fujian white tea
description.aroma: Honeyed, fruity, with hints of dried fruit
description.taste: Full-bodied, sweet, and honeyed, with noticeably more mouthfeel than Fujian white teas
description.processing: Plucking bud with leaf from large-leaf var. assamica trees → extended indoor shade-withering (avoiding direct sunlight to maintain the leaf color contrast) → slow drying

history.origin: A relatively modern style compared to classic Fujian white teas — developed in Yunnan as a regional adaptation of white tea processing using indigenous broad-leaf material.
history.development: Expanded commercially during the 2000s when Yunnan pu-erh producers began experimenting with alternative processing methods for large-leaf tea gardens.
history.modern: Today Yue Guang Bai is a well-established style distinct from classical Fujian white tea, celebrated for its unique two-toned leaf aesthetic and nectar-like flavor.
interestingFacts: The name 'Moonlight' refers to the visual appearance of the leaf (one side dark like the night sky, the other pale silvery like moonlight), not to any nocturnal harvesting ritual.
Thanks to the high polyphenol content of broad-leaf Yunnan varietals, Yue Guang Bai ages remarkably well, sharing aging traits with young sheng pu-erh.
